chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: Portrait, the Fanny show tune and Charlie Parker's absence
summary: String piece Portrait never released, a singers' show-tune project, and remarks on what Parker would do today.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: You ever heard that? I wrote for about 30 pieces.
On strings? Sue's still got it someplace.

Yeah, 'Portrait' is what I wrote. It was never released. That's right, Thad Jones did it. It was released with Thad Jones. Three or four vocalists were a guy who won [MOUTH] a whore, Celia, an Arthur Godfrey Award. Max's wife, (inaudible), she wanted this kid to produce (inaudible) it was going to be a big hit. So they did a show called Fanny. I think it was Fanny. Yeah, was there a show called 'Fanny?'
Yeah, there was a Broadway show called 'Fanny.'
In other words, you took a tune from the show and made an arrangement of it.

No, we were supposed to have this tune originally in (inaudible) the show. They lied, the guy (inaudible). well supposed to give it to us do this exclusively. And we'll just put a singer. That's -- what do you call them, Celia and Margo. They were going to have it exclusively. So we made it.
You could use the same track, or have them play it over again?
Yeah. It wasn't suitable to him. Charlie Parker would have been better.
Been better to have Charlie Parker play it.
Well, for almost anything it would be better to have Charlie Parker play it. I often wonder what would happen if Charlie Parker walked into the scene today, he'd blow everybody's head away.
He sure would. Even if he wasn't high. If weren't high,
Preferably he (inaudible), probably. How about I meant-alcohol? Bird drank a lot, he drank a lot, after he [fixed with] heroin, (inaudible).
